chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The people of the world are like travellers who are being carried while they are asleep.

key_terms.رَكْب: a caravan, a group of travelers

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor for worldly life in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this profound metaphor from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the spiritual heedlessness (ghaflah) of those engrossed in worldly pursuits, comparing them to travelers asleep in a caravan who are unaware of their destination. This imagery underscores the transient nature of dunya and the urgent need for self-reflection to awaken from the slumber of materialism before the final journey concludes.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 64. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him,
said: The people of the world are like travellers who are being carried while they are asleep.
